newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich looks forward to cooperation with Clinton.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich looks forward to cooperation with Clinton.

text.p: - House Speaker Newt Gingrich said Monday night that he led the applause during parts of President Clinton's State of the Union Speech because welfare reform and a balanced budget are also important to Republicans.
Gingrich told a $50-a-plate Lincoln Day dinner that when the President expressed his opposition to a balanced budget amendment, conservatives remained seated.
That is how the Republicans will approach President Clinton's budget and other legislation from his administration that comes before the new session of Congress, Gingrich said.

"We'll say, 'Tell me every good idea you've got and we'll try to pass them; and the ideas that aren't very good, we'll try to improve them; and the ideas we can't approve, we'll listen to you again next year,'" he said.
Gingrich said conservatives should have no reason to fear that the Republican Congress would work too closely with the President, as long as the Republicans remain steadfast in their ideals.
The four areas he intended to focus on are: race relations, creating a drug-free America, the elimination of ignorance, and the exaltation of religious faith, the House Speaker told the crowd.
